card.name: Ponung
card.tagline: Adi women's circle dance led by a singing Miri
card.profile: Ponung is the most iconic folk dance of the Adi people of Arunachal Pradesh, performed exclusively by women (typically unmarried girls) in vibrant traditional attire during the Solung harvest festival and other auspicious occasions (Wikipedia, Adi people; MyGov). The women form a circle, sometimes holding hands, moving in slow, graceful rhythmic steps, while a single male leader called the Miri stands at the centre singing folk songs that narrate the origin of crops, the history of the Adis and creation myths (auchitya; MyGov). The Miri also plays the Yoksha, a sword-shaped instrument with loosely attached iron discs that produce a rattling sound (auchitya; North East PSC).
card.insight: Solung derives from 'Eso' (mithun) and 'lung' (herd), and the Ponung dances are performed on its final days alongside the exchange of meat and gifts; the women's costume includes the Gale skirt, Galuk blouse and ornaments such as the Gol Pota, Madoli and Tampilang (Wikipedia, Adi people; MyGov).
card.image_significance: The Adi women's harvest myth-circle. A representative image shows ornate costume and expressive hand-gesture (mudra) detail — Arunachal (Adi), India.
